assertions: XChaCha20-Poly1305 journal envelope is not plaintext searchable
reopen preserves the pause latch and advances controller epoch
immutable Phase 1 snapshot and outbox digests are retained
all-zero keys are rejected
wrong keys fail authentication
tampered envelope digests and denormalized management mode fail closed
before-commit failpoint returns an explicit error
the previous pause projection remains after abort
the aborted event creates no orphaned outbox row
missing additive tables are repaired
missing journal data is not invented
a newer schema marker is refused
legacy read-only startup refuses an active management database
legacy read-only startup can inspect a disabled database
disabled mode remains represented in the durable journal
a snapshot identity cannot be overwritten with different bytes
WAL checkpoint and file-copy backup reopen successfully
the copied Phase 1 snapshot digest remains present
the committed encrypted journal reopens after the simulated lost reply
replaying the exact command returns its original receipt
no second revision is created
deterministic disk-full failpoint rejects the candidate transaction
the prior active revision and plan epoch remain authoritative
the failed transaction adds no outbox rows
audit/outbox append failpoint rejects before commit
the previous encrypted journal projection remains active
no orphaned outbox event is left after the failed append
post-commit acknowledgement loss still retains the new active revision
reopen reads the committed journal and unpublished outbox
replaying the exact projection does not duplicate outbox rows
restart preserves the durable pause latch
recovered status is paused_ready
recovery emits no input.submitted event or semantic resume
a deleted outbox row does not alter the authoritative journal
reconciliation persists the missing event from journal state
the rebuilt outbox count returns to the original bounded set
a 4097-event journal is rejected with journal_invalid
recovery does not materialize an over-bound event list

limits: deterministic transaction failpoint and reopen coverage, not an OS process-kill proof
no multi-process ownership fencing or native reservation evidence
no production key management, provider, game, deployment, or release rollback evidence
